messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@sparrowmd.com>
Date: 2028-06-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated reservation options and ramp worksheet for SparrowMD

Alex — attaching the reservation options we discussed on the call. High level first: I sketched three paths that match the usage profile you shared (heavy daytime inference, bursty QA runs overnight). Each option includes cluster sizing, the minimum GPU floor we recommend, and a pragmatic ramp schedule so you don't over-commit during model tuning. Attached: sparrowmd-reservation-options-v1.pdf (proposal) and runway-schedule-sheet.xlsx (lift/eval assumptions).

Quick summary of the three offers (details inside the PDF):
- Baseline Mesa: 12 GPUs (min-floor 6) — conservative cost, steady-state for production with 2x buffer for daytime peaks; 3-month ramp to full 12 GPUs.
- Elastic Spur: 18 GPUs (min-floor 8) — supports higher concurrency and overnight batch jobs; includes scheduled burst windows and soft preemption for non-critical batches; 2-month ramp.
- Anchored Ramp: 36 GPUs (min-floor 12) — long-term throughput posture with phased activation (12 -> 24 -> 36) over 6 months; includes warm standby nodes and SLA uplift.

Notes you asked for on the call: per-token unit economics in the PDF reflect usage smoothing across the ramp; burst pricing applies only within scheduled windows; we can include an 8-week pilot credit if you want to validate latency targets before committing.

Next steps: please review and flag which option is closest to what you want. If you like, we'll put together a two-week pilot MSA or a mutual action plan (MAP) and schedule a technical kickoff. Happy to hop on 30 minutes tomorrow if helpful.

—Hannah

2) We need to confirm burst windows are enforceable by schedule (not best-effort). Can we lock two 4-hour windows per weekday for guaranteed bursting?
3) For the 2-week pilot you mentioned, can we run it on 8xA10G equivalent GPUs (we have preference for that card family for parity with our local infra)?
4) What is the SLA uplift you referenced for Anchored Ramp (p50/p90 latency targets and uptime %) and what credits are available for missed targets?

I've looped Priya from procurement to start a MAP and make sure the contract approach will work with our SOW cadence. If you can answer these points I can push a short internal note to leadership.

Date: 2028-07-01T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation options and ramp worksheet for SparrowMD

Alex / Priya — thanks, great questions. Karthik from Capacity Planning is cc'd and added technical notes inline below. Answers are intentionally pragmatic to keep the pilot moving.

1) Warm standby billing: we offer a reduced "standby credit" for nodes that are kept warm (cached model/kernels loaded) but not actively billed at full compute. Practically: warm nodes count at ~40% of full GPU rate. If you need guaranteed compute availability (no spin-up) we can count them as full-rate reserved GPUs. Recommendation: for Elastic Spur use 4 warm standby nodes (billed at 40%) and allow scheduled burst to scale to reserved + burst at full rate.

2) Burst windows: yes — burst windows are enforceable. We can reserve two weekday windows (08:00-12:00, 18:00-22:00 local) as part of the policy. During those windows we move queued batch work onto higher-priority queues; SLA and billing reflect that choice.

3) Pilot hardware: we can allocate an 8x A10-equivalent pilot cluster. Pilot pricing: complimentary credits for 4 weeks (we recommend a 2-week active validation + 2-week buffer) — we'll cover the pilot capacity cost up to the credit limit. After pilot you can convert the pilot cluster to reserved capacity or decommission.

4) SLA uplift for Anchored Ramp: target p50 latency 80 ms, p90 210 ms for your daytime profile (under the documented concurrency assumptions); uptime objective 99.9% for reserved capacity. Credits: standard SLA credit ladder (5% invoice credit for monthly uptime 99.5-99.9, 15% for 99.0-99.5). If you need a stronger credit regime we can propose an enterprise SLA with different pricing.

Technical notes (from Karthik):
- Minimum GPU floors are primarily for cache/KV efficiencies; going below recommended min floors will cause higher per-token latency variability and lower batching efficiency.
- Autoscale: we support burst-to-hosted fallback when committed pool exhausted; fallback is configurable and can be gated by cost thresholds.
- Activation lead time: cold activation of a new GPU pod ~20-30 minutes; warm standby ~2-5 minutes.

Attached is the updated worksheet with the warm-standby rows filled (runway-schedule-sheet.xlsx). If the answers look good I'll prep a short MAP and draft an SOW.

—Hannah

Subject: Internal: SparrowMD concession ask + pilot credit approval (DEAL-2028-1437)

Marissa — quick internal note to secure approval for a modest pilot concession to keep momentum. Context: SparrowMD wants an 8x A10 pilot (2 weeks active) and explicit warm-standby billing at 40% for 4 nodes during Elastic Spur. They care about hard burst windows and an SLA uplift for Anchored Ramp.

Proposal: approve pilot credits covering up to 4 weeks of an 8x cluster (cap at $6k) and allow a one-time 10% introductory credit on month 1 of a committed anchor (if they convert within 60 days). We will keep the regular SLA credit ladder but offer to discuss enterprise SLA if they want stronger financials.

Rationale: this is a mid-size strategic customer with material ARR potential; the pilot will validate tail latency and open the path to a 36-GPU anchored committed contract. Without the concession we risk losing the pilot window to a competitor.

Karthik has added the warm-standby line items in the worksheet and confirmed activation lead-times. If you approve I will: (1) update the PDF and MAP, (2) send a signed pilot credit memo, and (3) run pricing through finance for final sign-off. Attach discount-term-sheet.pdf as the proposed language.

Approve?

—Hannah
